source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
A monthly planting/harvest calendar (based on the 250-household survey) shows corn planting and harvest windows differ notably by province:

Kampong Cham (53 households): planting concentrated April-June; harvest concentrated July-October.

Kandal (73 households): planting spread across January-June plus a December window (suggesting farmers there run more than one crop cycle per year); harvest spread April-September.

Battambang (69 households): planting in January and again June-August; harvest concentrated September-December (extending later into the year than other provinces).

Pailin (55 households): planting February-April; harvest June-October.

The document notes farmers in mountainous areas (like parts of Battambang/Pailin) typically start planting in April and harvest around October, while farmers on flat/lowland terrain (like Kandal) plant around June and harvest around September. Kandal farmers who plant early (April) can harvest as early as August, while those planting in June harvest around September. Battambang farmers who plant mid-year harvest around November-December, while those in Pailin can complete their full cycle (planting to harvest) within a single year, sometimes across three staggered plots timed roughly a month apart.
